questions.stem: The mass of an object can be measured using the following instruments except
questions.explanation: A metre rule measures length; balances (and a lever balance) can be used to compare or measure mass.

questions.stem: A load of 80 N extends a spring by 8 cm. When the load is replaced by a copper block, the extension produced is 10 cm. Calculate the weight of the copper block, assuming that the elastic limit of the spring is not exceeded.
questions.explanation: By Hooke's law k = 80/8 = 10 N per cm, so W = 10 x 10 = 100 N.

questions.stem: A sample of air weighing 1.32 x 10^3 N is confined in a room measuring 9.5 m x 5.0 m x 2.0 m. Calculate the density of the sample. [g = 10 ms^-2]
A turkey stands and makes 4 x 10^-2 m^2 of contact with the ground. If the pressure it exerts on the ground is 2.8 x 10^3 Pa, calculate its weight.
questions.explanation: Weight = pressure x area = 2.8 x 10^3 x 4 x 10^-2 = 112 N.

questions.stem: A velocity-time graph shows the motions of two cars P and Q over a period of time t: each is a horizontal straight line, with the line for car P above the line for car Q. Which of the following statements about the motion of the cars is correct? P
options: has more horse power than Q.
has the same acceleration as Q.
and Q increase their speeds steadily.
questions.explanation: Horizontal lines on a velocity-time graph mean constant velocity, so both cars have zero acceleration - the same acceleration.

questions.stem: When a projectile is projected with an initial velocity U at an angle theta to the horizontal, the horizontal component of its velocity is
questions.explanation: Resolving U along the horizontal gives U cos theta.

questions.topic: Second Law: force, acceleration, momentum and impulse
questions.stem: A body of mass 200 g moving at 15.0 ms^-1 is accelerated to 25.0 ms^-1 in a time of 10.0 s. Determine the magnitude of the accelerating force.
A body of mass 200 g moving at 15.0 ms^-1 is accelerated to 25.0 ms^-1 in a time of 10.0 s. Calculate the amount of work done on the body.
questions.explanation: Work done = change in K.E. = 1/2 x 0.2 x (25^2 - 15^2) = 40 J.

questions.stem: The magnitude of the resultant of two forces inclined at an angle of 30 degrees is
options: greater than the magnitude of either force.
equal to the sum of the magnitudes of the two forces.
equal to the difference in the magnitudes of the two forces.
greater than the sum of the magnitudes of the two forces.
questions.explanation: R^2 = F1^2 + F2^2 + 2F1F2 cos 30 is larger than F1^2 or F2^2 but less than (F1 + F2)^2, so R exceeds either force but not their sum.

questions.stem: A uniform metre rule balances horizontally when it is pivoted at the 70 cm mark and a mass of 105 g is suspended at the 90 cm mark. Calculate the mass of the metre rule.
questions.explanation: The weight acts at the 50 cm mark: m x 20 = 105 x 20, so m = 105 g.

questions.topic: Illustration, explanation and definition of simple harmonic motion
questions.stem: Which of the following motions is not simple harmonic?
options: The motion of a particle in a transverse wave
The vibrating prongs of a tuning fork
A simple pendulum swinging with large angular amplitude
The vertical vibrations of a mass at the end of a spring
questions.explanation: A pendulum is only approximately simple harmonic for small angular amplitudes.

questions.topic: Period, frequency and amplitude of S.H.M.
questions.stem: A pendulum clock keeps a wrong time when the room temperature rises substantially. This observation is due to
options: an increase in the period as a result of an increase in the length of the pendulum.
a decrease in the period due to an increase in the length of the pendulum.
an increase in the period due to a decrease in the length of the pendulum.
a decrease in the period due to a decrease in the length of the pendulum.
questions.explanation: Heat expands the pendulum rod, and T = 2 pi sqrt(l/g) increases, so the clock loses time.

questions.stem: Jet and rocket propulsions are based on
questions.explanation: The exhaust gases are pushed backwards and react by pushing the jet or rocket forwards (action and reaction).

questions.topic: Structure of matter (kinetic theory and diffusion)
questions.stem: When the average separation of the molecules of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is increased, there is corresponding average
options: increase in the rate of collisions.
decrease in pressure of the gas.
increase in kinetic energy of the gas.
decrease in the number of molecules.
questions.explanation: Greater separation means larger volume, so fewer collisions per unit area per second and lower pressure.

questions.stem: A force of 25 N, acting at 60 degrees to the horizontal, pulls a block along a horizontal surface from point A to point B, a distance of 3.2 m. Calculate the lifting force acting on the block.
questions.explanation: Lifting (vertical) component = 25 sin 60 = 21.7 N.

questions.stem: A force of 25 N, acting at 60 degrees to the horizontal, pulls a block along a horizontal surface from point A to point B, a distance of 3.2 m. Calculate the work done in moving the block to point B.
A student pulls a trolley with a horizontal force of 50.0 N through a distance of 1.5 km in 20 minutes. Calculate the average power of the student.
When a bicycle is being ridden uphill, its mechanical advantage is
questions.explanation: A bicycle is a speed (distance) multiplier: the effort exceeds the load it overcomes, so its M.A. is less than 1.

questions.stem: The S.I unit of temperature is
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin (K).

questions.stem: Which of the following applications is not related to thermal expansion?
options: Anomalous expansion of water from 0 degrees C to 4 degrees C
questions.explanation: Between 0 and 4 degrees C water contracts on heating (anomalous behaviour); the others are applications of expansion on heating.

questions.stem: An air bubble of volume 4 x 10^-6 m^3, formed 5 m below water surface, moves upward. Determine its volume just before it reaches the surface. (Assume that the temperature remains constant, atmospheric pressure equals 10 m of water)
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: 15 x 4 x 10^-6 = 10 x V, so V = 6.0 x 10^-6 m^3.

questions.stem: An aluminium calorimeter without a lid and jacket is placed on a table. Boiling water is then poured into it. Which of the following processes will account for the cooling of the water? I. Conduction II. Evaporation III. Radiation IV. Convection
questions.explanation: With no lid or jacket, heat is lost by conduction to the table, evaporation from the open surface, radiation and convection currents in the air.

questions.stem: The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by 1 degree C is known as
questions.explanation: That is the definition of specific heat capacity.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations does not represent a travelling wave?
questions.explanation: A travelling wave varies as sin(omega t - kx); T/t is not a linear phase in t, so option C is not a progressive wave equation.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at plane surfaces
questions.stem: The refractive indices of water and glass with respect to air are 4/3 and 3/2 respectively. If the speed of white light in glass is 2.00 x 10^8 ms^-1, calculate its speed in water.
Optical fibres are based on the principle of
questions.explanation: Light is trapped in the fibre by repeated total internal reflection.

questions.topic: Refraction of light at curved surfaces
questions.stem: When an object is placed 12 cm from a converging lens, a real image four times its original size is produced. Calculate the focal length of the lens.

Which of the following statements about sound waves are correct? I. In a uniform medium, the intensity of sound waves is directly proportional to the distance from the source. II. The amplitude of sound waves of given frequency and wave length is a measure of the energy of the waves. III. Pitch is the effect of frequency of sound waves on the human ear.
questions.explanation: Intensity falls off as the inverse square of distance, so I is false; II and III are true.

questions.topic: Application of lenses in optical instruments
questions.stem: For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the distance between the lenses is
questions.explanation: In normal adjustment the principal foci coincide, so the separation is fo + fe.

questions.stem: The pitch of a musical note depends on
questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by frequency.

questions.stem: Two sonometer wires, X and Y, have the same length. If the mass per unit length of X is 1/9 that of Y, determine the ratio of the frequency of X to that of Y.
questions.explanation: f is proportional to 1/sqrt(mu) (same length and tension), so fX/fY = sqrt(9) = 3 : 1.

questions.topic: Vibration of air in pipes: open and closed pipes
questions.stem: The first resonant length of the air column vibrating to a tuning fork in a closed tube is 26.25 cm. Neglecting end correction, calculate the frequency of the fork. [Speed of sound in air = 336 ms^-1]
questions.explanation: L = lambda/4, so lambda = 1.05 m and f = 336/1.05 = 320 Hz.

questions.topic: Gravitational force between two masses: Newton's law of gravitation
questions.stem: The derived unit for the universal gravitational constant G is
questions.explanation: G = F r^2 / (m1 m2), so its unit is N m^2 kg^-2.

questions.stem: Static electricity is produced by either loss or gain of
questions.explanation: Bodies become charged by losing or gaining electrons.

questions.stem: An insulated negatively charged rod is held high above the cap of a positively charged electroscope. The rod is slowly moved down towards the cap until it is just above it. The leaves of the electroscope will be observed to slowly
questions.explanation: Electrons repelled into the leaves first neutralise their positive charge (collapse) and then make them negative (diverge again).

questions.stem: A total charge of 1.0 millicoulomb is stored by the capacitors in a circuit in which a capacitor of X microfarad and a 2 microfarad capacitor are connected in parallel across a 100 V battery. Calculate the value of X.
questions.explanation: C = Q/V = 1.0 x 10^-3 / 100 = 10 microfarad = X + 2, so X = 8 microfarad.

questions.stem: Electrical energy stored in a capacitor is given by the expression
A 120 ohm resistor is connected across an a.c. having a maximum voltage of 283 V. Calculate the rms value of the current in the circuit.

questions.topic: Measurement of electric current, p.d., resistance, e.m.f. and internal resistance of a cell
questions.stem: In a Wheatstone bridge connected to a 20 V supply, the four arms are 10 ohm and 7.5 ohm (upper pair) and 12 ohm and R (lower pair), with the 10 ohm and 12 ohm arms on the same side and a galvanometer G joining the two midpoints. Determine the value of R at null deflection.
questions.explanation: At balance 10/7.5 = 12/R, so R = 9 ohm.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is the most effective for making a magnet?
options: Hammering in the earth's magnetic field
questions.explanation: Using a solenoid carrying direct current gives the strongest magnetisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors does not increase the strength of an induced emf in a solenoid? The
options: polarity of the magnet facing the solenoid
speed at which the magnet moves
number of turns of the solenoid
questions.explanation: The polarity only decides the direction of the induced emf, not its magnitude.

questions.topic: Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor and between parallel conductors
questions.stem: Two identical parallel conductors close to each other carry equal currents in the same direction. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Each of the conductors will experience a force
Each of the conductors can move
The magnitudes of the forces on the conductors will be equal
The two conductors will repel each other
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction attract each other.

questions.stem: In the wiring of houses, the switch is connected to the
options: earth and neutral wires bridged together.
questions.explanation: Switches go in the live wire so that the appliance is dead when switched off.

questions.stem: A circuit consisting of a resistor R, an inductor L and a capacitor C in series is connected to an alternating current source. At resonance, the
questions.explanation: At resonance XL = XC, the impedance is minimum (= R) and the current is maximum.

questions.stem: Which of the following radiations is not part of the electromagnetic spectrum?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are helium nuclei, not electromagnetic waves.

questions.stem: Which of the following constituents of an atom enables matter to conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Conduction is by the movement of (free) electrons.

questions.stem: Radium (Ra) disintegrates as illustrated in the equation below. Identify particles X and Y. 222/88 Ra -> 217/86 Rn + 4/2 X + 1/0 Y
questions.explanation: 4/2 X is an alpha particle (helium nucleus) and 1/0 Y, with mass 1 and no charge, is a neutron.

questions.stem: It is not very possible to determine, exactly and simultaneously, both the position and momentum of a particle. This statement is called the
questions.explanation: This is Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.

questions.topic: Equations of motion with constant acceleration
questions.stem: A stone is projected vertically upward with a speed of 30 ms^-1 from the top of a tower of height 50 m. Neglecting air resistance, determine the time of flight on reaching the ground. [g = 10 ms^-2]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Taking upward as positive, s = -50 m: -50 = 30t - 5t^2
1 mark: t^2 - 6t - 10 = 0, so t = 3 + sqrt(19)
1 mark: t = 7.36 s (about 7.4 s)

questions.stem: A body of mass 0.5 kg is thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 25 ms^-1. Calculate the potential energy of the body at the maximum height reached. [g = 10 ms^-2]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: At maximum height all the kinetic energy has become potential energy
1 mark: P.E. = (1/2)mv^2 = (1/2) x 0.5 x 25^2
1 mark: = 156.25 J (about 156 J)
questions.explanation: At maximum height K.E. is fully converted: P.E. = (1/2)(0.5)(25)^2 = 156.25 J (equivalently h = 31.25 m and mgh = 156.25 J).

questions.stem: List two: (a) types of waves, other than light, that can be plane polarized; (b) methods of polarizing an unpolarized light.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Any two transverse waves other than light, e.g. radio waves/microwaves, X-rays, waves on a string
1 mark: (b) First method, e.g. using a polaroid (selective absorption)
1 mark: (b) Second method, e.g. reflection (at the Brewster angle), double refraction or scattering
questions.explanation: (a) Radio waves (microwaves) and waves on a stretched string/rope (any transverse waves). (b) Passing it through a polaroid sheet; reflection from a glass or water surface at the polarising angle (also double refraction in calcite, scattering).

questions.stem: (a) What is electrolysis? (b) A current of 2 A is passed through a copper voltameter for 5 minutes. Determine the mass of the copper deposited. [Electrochemical equivalent of copper = 3.27 x 10^-7 kg C^-1]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) The chemical decomposition of an electrolyte (in solution or molten) by passing an electric current through it
1 mark: (b) m = zIt = 3.27 x 10^-7 x 2 x 300
1 mark: m = 1.96 x 10^-4 kg
questions.explanation: (a) Electrolysis is the decomposition of a compound in molten or aqueous form by an electric current. (b) m = zIt = 3.27 x 10^-7 x 2 x (5 x 60) = 1.96 x 10^-4 kg.

questions.stem: State two: (a) differences; (b) similarities between thermionic and photoelectric emission.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Thermionic emission is caused by heating the metal; photoelectric emission by light (electromagnetic radiation) of suitable frequency falling on it
1 mark: (a) Thermionic emission occurs from heated cathodes of any metal at high temperature; photoemission needs frequency above the threshold frequency and is instantaneous / used in photocells vs. CRO, X-ray tubes
1 mark: (b) Both emit electrons from a metal surface; both require the electrons to gain energy at least equal to the work function
questions.explanation: Differences: thermionic emission uses heat energy whereas photoelectric emission uses light energy; photoemission depends on frequency exceeding a threshold, thermionic emission on temperature. Similarities: both release electrons from metal surfaces, and in both the electron must acquire energy greater than the work function of the metal.

questions.stem: The table below shows the pointer reading of a spring balance when different weights are hung on it. Determine the value of F. Weight / N: 5, 10, F. Pointer reading / cm: 8, 12, 30.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Extension per newton = (12 - 8)/(10 - 5) = 0.8 cm per N
1 mark: Zero (unloaded) reading = 8 - 5 x 0.8 = 4 cm
1 mark: 30 = 4 + 0.8F, so F = 32.5 N
questions.explanation: The reading rises by 4 cm for 5 N (0.8 cm per N), so the unloaded reading is 4 cm. Then 30 - 4 = 26 cm corresponds to 26/0.8 = 32.5 N.

questions.stem: An x-ray tube operates at a potential of 2500 V. If the power of the tube is 750 W, calculate the current passing through the tube.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: P = IV
1 mark: I = 750/2500
1 mark: I = 0.3 A

questions.topic: Structure of matter (kinetic theory and diffusion)
questions.stem: Using the kinetic theory, explain the rise of water in a glass capillary tube.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Water molecules are attracted to the glass molecules (adhesion)
1 mark: The adhesive force between water and glass is greater than the cohesive force between water molecules
1 mark: So water wets the glass and is pulled up the narrow tube (concave meniscus) until the weight of the column balances the surface tension force
questions.explanation: The adhesive force between water molecules and glass molecules is greater than the cohesive force between water molecules. Water therefore spreads up the glass, forming a concave meniscus, and the surface tension pulls the column up the narrow bore until its weight balances the upward pull.

questions.stem: Explain briefly the principle of action of a discharge tube.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: A gas at low pressure is placed between two electrodes and a high p.d. is applied
1 mark: Electrons/ions are accelerated and collide with gas atoms, exciting or ionizing them
1 mark: The excited atoms return to lower energy levels and emit light of characteristic colours (frequencies)
questions.explanation: A discharge tube contains a gas at low pressure between two electrodes across which a high voltage is applied. Free electrons and ions are accelerated and collide with gas atoms, exciting or ionizing them; as the atoms fall back to lower energy levels they emit light of wavelengths characteristic of the gas.

questions.stem: Write down the name of: (a) two particles used in explaining the wave nature of matter; (b) one device whose invention is based on the wave nature of matter.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) First particle, e.g. electron
1 mark: (a) Second particle, e.g. neutron (or proton/alpha particle)
1 mark: (b) Electron microscope
questions.explanation: (a) Electrons and neutrons (both show diffraction). (b) The electron microscope.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] The initial and final speeds of a moving object are u and v respectively. If the acceleration of the object is a and its time of motion is t, show that the expression v = u + at is dimensionally correct.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: [v] = [u] = LT^-1
1 mark: [at] = LT^-2 x T = LT^-1
1 mark: Every term has dimensions LT^-1, so the equation is dimensionally consistent
questions.explanation: Dimensions of v and u are LT^-1. Dimensions of at are (LT^-2)(T) = LT^-1. Since each term has the same dimensions, v = u + at is dimensionally correct.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] Two tuning forks of slightly different frequencies f1 and f2 are sounded together. Explain how audible beats are formed.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: The two waves superpose (interfere) as they travel together
1 mark: Because the frequencies differ slightly, they are alternately in phase (constructive - loud) and out of phase (destructive - soft)
1 mark: The periodic rise and fall of loudness is heard as beats with beat frequency f1 - f2
questions.explanation: The waves from the two forks superpose. Since their frequencies differ slightly, they drift in and out of phase: in phase they reinforce (loud sound), out of phase they cancel (soft sound). This regular waxing and waning of loudness, at a frequency of |f1 - f2|, is heard as beats.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] An engine transfers 2.00 x 10^3 J of energy from a hot reservoir during a cycle and transfers 1.50 x 10^3 J to a cold reservoir. Calculate the efficiency of the engine.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Work done = 2.00 x 10^3 - 1.50 x 10^3 = 500 J
1 mark: Efficiency = work done / heat input = 500/2000
1 mark: = 0.25 or 25%
questions.explanation: Useful work = 2000 - 1500 = 500 J. Efficiency = 500/2000 x 100% = 25%.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] The formula (P + a/V^2)(V - b) = RT represents van der Waal's equation. Explain how the extra terms a/V^2 and b account for the deviation from the ideal gas situation.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: a/V^2 corrects the pressure for intermolecular attractive forces, which an ideal gas ignores
1 mark: These attractions reduce the pressure exerted on the walls, so a/V^2 is added to the measured pressure
1 mark: b corrects the volume for the finite volume occupied by the molecules themselves, so the free volume is V - b
questions.explanation: Real gas molecules attract one another, which reduces the force with which they hit the walls; a/V^2 is added to P to correct for this. Real molecules also occupy a finite volume, so the space available for their motion is less than V; b is subtracted to give the free volume.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] A satellite of mass Ms situated at a height h above the surface of the earth moves with a speed Vs in circular orbit around the earth. If the mass and radius of the earth are Me and Re respectively and the gravitational constant is G, write down an expression for the magnitude of the: (a) centripetal force needed to maintain the satellite in orbit. (b) gravitational field strength in the region of the satellite.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) F = Ms Vs^2 / (Re + h)
1 mark: (a) (equivalently F = G Me Ms / (Re + h)^2, since gravity supplies the centripetal force)
1 mark: (b) g = G Me / (Re + h)^2
questions.explanation: (a) F = Ms Vs^2/(Re + h), which equals G Me Ms/(Re + h)^2. (b) g = G Me/(Re + h)^2.

questions.topic: Magnetic force on a moving charged particle
questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] List three devices in everyday life which operate on the deflection of electric charges in a magnetic field.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: e.g. television (cathode-ray) tube
1 mark: e.g. moving-coil loudspeaker / electric motor
1 mark: e.g. moving-coil galvanometer/ammeter, mass spectrometer
questions.explanation: Cathode-ray television tube, electric motor (and moving-coil loudspeaker), moving-coil meters.

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] In a circuit, a 9 V battery is connected in series with a 15 ohm resistor; the other end of the 15 ohm resistor joins a 20 ohm resistor and a 12 ohm resistor which are in parallel with each other and both return to the battery. Using Kirchhoff's rule, determine the current through each resistor.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Total resistance = 15 + (20 x 12)/(20 + 12) = 22.5 ohm; current through 15 ohm = 9/22.5 = 0.4 A
1 mark: p.d. across parallel pair = 9 - 0.4 x 15 = 3 V; current through 20 ohm = 3/20 = 0.15 A
1 mark: current through 12 ohm = 3/12 = 0.25 A (0.15 + 0.25 = 0.4 A by the junction rule)
questions.explanation: Parallel combination = 7.5 ohm, total 22.5 ohm, I = 0.4 A in the 15 ohm resistor. The p.d. across the parallel pair is 3 V, so 0.15 A flows in the 20 ohm resistor and 0.25 A in the 12 ohm resistor (0.15 + 0.25 = 0.4 A).

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] State three properties of an intrinsic semiconductor.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: It is a pure semiconductor (e.g. pure silicon or germanium) with no added impurity
1 mark: The number of free electrons equals the number of holes
1 mark: Its conductivity is low at room temperature and increases with temperature (negative temperature coefficient of resistance)
questions.explanation: An intrinsic semiconductor is pure (undoped); it has equal numbers of electrons and holes; its conductivity is small but increases as temperature rises (resistance falls).

questions.stem: [For candidates in Ghana] With the aid of diagrams, explain what is meant by (a) forward bias; (b) reverse bias.
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) p-side connected to the positive terminal and n-side to the negative terminal of the battery (diagram)
1 mark: (a) Depletion layer narrows and a large current flows
1 mark: (b) p-side connected to negative and n-side to positive; depletion layer widens and only a very small leakage current flows
questions.explanation: (a) Forward bias: the p-type side of the p-n junction is joined to the positive terminal and the n-type side to the negative terminal; the barrier potential and depletion layer are reduced and the diode conducts. (b) Reverse bias: the connections are reversed; the depletion layer widens and practically no current flows (only a tiny leakage current).

questions.stem: (a)(i) Explain relative motion. [2 marks] (ii) Two cars moving in opposite directions on the same straight road with velocities 80 km h^-1 and 60 km h^-1 respectively pass each other at a point. Determine the velocity of the first car relative to the second. [2 marks] (b)(i) Define force. [1 mark] (ii) Classify the following forces as either contact forces or field forces: push; tension; gravitational; electrostatic; reaction and magnetic. [3 marks] (c) A body starts from rest and travels in a straight line for 2 seconds with uniform acceleration of 1 ms^-2. It then travels at a constant speed for some time before coming to rest with a uniform retardation of 2 ms^-2. The total distance covered by it is 15 m. (i) Draw and label a velocity-time graph for the motion. (ii) Calculate the: (A) velocity attained after the first 2 seconds; (B) total time taken for the journey. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Relative motion is the motion of a body as observed from another body which may itself be moving (velocity of A relative to B = vA - vB)
1 mark: (a)(ii) v = 80 - (-60)
1 mark: = 140 km h^-1 in the direction of the first car
1 mark: (b)(i) Force is that which changes or tends to change the state of rest or uniform motion of a body
2 marks: (b)(ii) Contact forces: push, tension, reaction
1 mark: (b)(ii) Field forces: gravitational, electrostatic, magnetic
2 marks: (c)(i) Correctly labelled v-t graph: rising line from 0 to 2 m/s in 2 s, horizontal line, falling line to zero
1 mark: (c)(ii)(A) v = u + at = 0 + 1 x 2 = 2 ms^-1
1 mark: Distance in acceleration = 2 m and in retardation = 2^2/(2 x 2) = 1 m (time 1 s)
2 marks: Constant-speed distance = 15 - 3 = 12 m, time = 12/2 = 6 s
1 mark: (c)(ii)(B) Total time = 2 + 6 + 1 = 9 s
questions.explanation: (a) Relative motion is the motion of one body as seen from another; the velocity of A relative to B is vA - vB. Taking the first car's direction as positive, 80 - (-60) = 140 km/h. (b) Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change a body's state of rest or uniform motion. Contact: push, tension, reaction. Field: gravitational, electrostatic, magnetic. (c) The v-t graph rises from 0 to 2 m/s in 2 s, stays at 2 m/s, then falls to 0. v = 0 + 1 x 2 = 2 m/s. Areas: 2 m (first 2 s) + 1 m (1 s retardation) leaves 12 m at 2 m/s, i.e. 6 s. Total time = 9 s.

questions.stem: (a)(i) What is mechanical energy? [2 marks] (ii) A ball of mass M raised to a height H above the ground is allowed to fall freely towards the ground. Show that at a point T when it has fallen through a distance h, the total mechanical energy remains unchanged. [4 marks] (b)(i) What is a thermometric property? [2 marks] (ii) Copy and complete the table below (columns: thermometric substance, thermometric property, kind of thermometer): Mercury / ___ / Liquid-in-glass; ___ / ___ / Platinium resistance; Gas / Pressure / ___; ___ / ___ / Thermocouple. [3 marks] (c) An inclined plane is used to raise a box 25.0 kg to the top of the plane by an effort of 180 N. Assuming the plane is 60% efficient, calculate the: (i) mechanical advantage; (ii) velocity ratio; (iii) angle the plane makes with the horizontal. [g = 10 ms^-2] [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Mechanical energy is the sum of the kinetic and potential energies of a body (energy due to motion or position)
1 mark: (a)(ii) At the top: P.E. = MgH, K.E. = 0, total = MgH
1 mark: At T: P.E. = Mg(H - h)
1 mark: v^2 = 2gh, so K.E. = (1/2)M(2gh) = Mgh
1 mark: Total at T = Mg(H - h) + Mgh = MgH, unchanged
2 marks: (b)(i) A physical property of a substance that changes continuously and measurably with temperature
1 mark: (b)(ii) Mercury - change in volume/length of the thread; platinum - electrical resistance
1 mark: Gas - pressure - constant-volume gas thermometer
1 mark: Thermocouple - two dissimilar metals (e.g. copper and iron) - e.m.f. (thermoelectric e.m.f.)
1 mark: (c)(i) M.A. = load/effort = 250/180 = 1.39
1 mark: (c)(ii) V.R. = M.A./efficiency = 1.39/0.6 = 2.31
1 mark: (c)(iii) V.R. = 1/sin theta, so sin theta = 1/2.31 = 0.432
1 mark: theta = 25.6 degrees
questions.explanation: (a) Mechanical energy is the total of a body's kinetic and potential energy. At the start, E = MgH. After falling h, P.E. = Mg(H - h) and, from v^2 = 2gh, K.E. = Mgh; the total is MgH, so it is conserved. (b) A thermometric property varies continuously with temperature (e.g. length of a liquid column, resistance, pressure, e.m.f.). Table: mercury - volume expansion; platinum - resistance (platinum resistance thermometer); gas - pressure - constant-volume gas thermometer; two different metals - thermoelectric e.m.f. - thermocouple. (c) Load = 250 N, M.A. = 250/180 = 1.39; V.R. = 1.39/0.6 = 2.31; sin theta = 1/V.R. = 0.432, theta = 25.6 degrees.

questions.stem: (a)(i) Explain interference of waves. [2 marks] (ii) With the aid of diagrams distinguish between constructive and destructive interference of transverse waves. [4 marks] (b) A stretched wire under tension T produces a note of frequency 60 Hz when plucked. Calculate the frequency if the tension in the wire is increased by 125%. [4 marks] (c) The displacement of a plane progressive wave is given by the equation y = 12.5 sin (240 pi t - 0.50 pi x), where the symbols have their usual meanings, y and x are in metres and t in seconds. For the wave, determine the: (i) frequency; (ii) wavelength; (iii) speed. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Interference is the superposition of two (coherent) waves meeting at a point to give a resultant displacement equal to the sum of the individual displacements
2 marks: (a)(ii) Constructive: waves meet in phase (crest on crest), giving a resultant of larger amplitude (diagram)
2 marks: Destructive: waves meet in antiphase (crest on trough), giving reduced or zero amplitude (diagram)
1 mark: (b) f is proportional to sqrt(T)
1 mark: New tension = T + 1.25T = 2.25T
1 mark: f2 = 60 x sqrt(2.25)
1 mark: f2 = 90 Hz
1 mark: (c)(i) 2 pi f = 240 pi
1 mark: f = 120 Hz
1 mark: (c)(ii) 2 pi/lambda = 0.50 pi
1 mark: lambda = 4.0 m
1 mark: (c)(iii) v = f lambda = 120 x 4 = 480 ms^-1
questions.explanation: (a) Interference is the superposition of coherent waves to give a resultant displacement equal to the algebraic sum of the individual displacements. Constructive: waves in phase, crest meets crest, larger amplitude. Destructive: waves in antiphase, crest meets trough, reduced or zero amplitude. (b) f is proportional to sqrt(T); T becomes 2.25T, so f = 60 x 1.5 = 90 Hz. (c) Comparing with y = A sin(2 pi f t - 2 pi x/lambda): f = 120 Hz, lambda = 4.0 m, v = 480 m/s.

questions.topic: Production of electric current from primary and secondary cells
questions.stem: (a) State two advantages and one disadvantage of alkaline cells over lead-acid cells. [3 marks] (b) Explain why High-Tension transmission of power is done with low current and high voltage. [3 marks] (c) A uniform potentiometer wire AB of length 100 cm and resistance 2 ohm is connected in series with a cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V, a variable resistor R and a key K1. A cell of e.m.f. 0.08 V, a galvanometer G and a key K2 are connected between A and a sliding contact J on the wire. If R = 4 ohm and the key K1 is closed, calculate the (i) current in the potentiometer circuit; (ii) length AJ of the wire for which the galvanometer shows no deflection, when key K2 is also closed. [6 marks] (d) A heating coil is rated at 70 W. Calculate the time it will take this coil to heat 1.4 kg of water at 30 degrees C to 100 degrees C. [Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1] [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Advantage: alkaline cells are lighter / more portable
1 mark: Advantage: they are more robust, can deliver/stand heavy currents and have a longer life; need little maintenance (no acid spillage)
1 mark: Disadvantage: they have a lower e.m.f. per cell (about 1.2 V) / are more expensive
1 mark: (b) Power loss in the cables is I^2 R
1 mark: For a given power P = IV, a high voltage means a small current
1 mark: so the I^2 R heating loss in the transmission lines is minimised (thinner, cheaper cables can be used)
1 mark: (c)(i) I = E/(R + r_wire) = 1.5/(4 + 2)
1 mark: I = 0.25 A
1 mark: (c)(ii) p.d. across wire = 0.25 x 2 = 0.5 V over 100 cm
1 mark: p.d. per cm = 0.005 V cm^-1
1 mark: AJ = 0.08/0.005
1 mark: AJ = 16 cm
1 mark: (d) Heat needed = mc(theta2 - theta1) = 1.4 x 4200 x 70 = 411 600 J
1 mark: Pt = mc(delta theta), t = 411 600/70
1 mark: t = 5880 s (98 minutes)
questions.explanation: (a) Alkaline cells are lighter and more durable, can supply large currents without damage and need little maintenance; but their e.m.f. per cell is lower (about 1.2 V) and they are more expensive. (b) Line loss is I^2 R; transmitting a given power at high voltage requires only a small current, so heat losses in the cables are minimised. (c) I = 1.5/6 = 0.25 A; the wire has 0.5 V across 100 cm (0.005 V/cm), so balance length AJ = 0.08/0.005 = 16 cm. (d) 70t = 1.4 x 4200 x 70, so t = 5880 s.

questions.stem: (a) Can other elements besides uranium be used in nuclear fission reactions? Give a reason for your answer. [2 marks] (b) A radioactive element has a half-life of 5 years. A detector placed near the element records an initial count rate of 4000 min^-1 as stated in the table below. t / years: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20; Count rate / min: 4000, ___, ___, ___, ___. (i) Copy and complete the table. (ii) Plot a graph with count rate on the vertical axis and t on the horizontal axis. (iii) Using the graph, determine the count rate at t = 12 years. (iv) List two detectors of radioactive radiations. [8 marks] (c) An energy-level diagram for a certain atom shows levels E0 = -15.4 eV, E1 = -10.1 eV, E2 = -5.6 eV and E3 = -3.3 eV. Transition A is from E1 to E0, transition B is from E2 to E0, transition C is from E3 to E0 and transition D is from E1 up to E2. (i) Which of the transitions A, B and C produces radiation with the shortest wavelength? Give a reason for your answer. (ii) An electron jumps from E0 to E2 by absorbing light energy. Calculate the wavelength of the light used. [h = 6.6 x 10^-34 Js; c = 3.0 x 10^8 ms^-1; 1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J] [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) Yes, e.g. plutonium (Pu-239) or thorium
1 mark: Any heavy nucleus that splits into lighter nuclei with release of energy when bombarded by neutrons can be used
2 marks: (b)(i) 2000, 1000, 500, 250 counts per minute
2 marks: (b)(ii) Correct axes, scales and smooth exponential decay curve through the points
2 marks: (b)(iii) Count rate at 12 years read from graph, about 760 min^-1 (accept 740-780)
2 marks: (b)(iv) Any two: Geiger-Muller counter, cloud chamber, spark counter, scintillation counter, photographic plate, ionization chamber
1 mark: (c)(i) C
1 mark: It has the largest energy difference (12.1 eV) and lambda = hc/E is smallest for largest E
1 mark: (c)(ii) Energy absorbed = -5.6 - (-15.4) = 9.8 eV = 9.8 x 1.6 x 10^-19 J
1 mark: lambda = hc/E = (6.6 x 10^-34 x 3.0 x 10^8)/(1.568 x 10^-18)
1 mark: lambda = 1.26 x 10^-7 m
questions.explanation: (a) Yes - e.g. plutonium-239 or thorium; any heavy nucleus that splits when struck by neutrons, releasing energy, can be used. (b) Count rates 2000, 1000, 500, 250 per minute at 5, 10, 15, 20 years; from the decay curve the rate at 12 years is about 760 per minute (calculated 757.9). Detectors: Geiger-Muller counter, cloud chamber (also spark counter, scintillation counter). (c) C, because E3 to E0 is the largest energy change (12.1 eV) and wavelength is inversely proportional to energy. For E0 to E2, E = 9.8 eV = 1.568 x 10^-18 J, lambda = hc/E = 1.26 x 10^-7 m.
